verdict.root_cause: checkoutservice is waiting, not failing. Its error ratio in the incident window is far below baseline with no sustained upward departure [tr_90ad52897faf], its logs show no errors and no restart, and PlaceOrder intake continues steadily through 23:42:47 while late-window orders stop at the order-start line with no payment/email/queue follow-up, for both USD and CAD [tr_180605051f30]. Traces localise the only large stall to cartservice's Redis operations: GetCart's HGET (~301ms) and EmptyCart's HMSET (~305ms) in a 640ms outlier against a 22-25ms norm, each carrying its duration as self-time, with checkout parent spans inflating purely by waiting and all other legs at a few milliseconds [tr_138e08c49752]. GetCart sits before the payment step, exactly where the log sequence now truncates. Most probable cause: cartservice's Redis-backed cart operations became slow and checkout orders hang in the cart phase. No change record supports a competing trigger on checkoutservice [tr_56d2719f6cfa] or paymentservice [tr_1f627744be3e].
verdict.reasoning: Metrics rule out an error surge at checkoutservice and rule out a sustained downstream hard-failure signature, since persistent RPC errors would hold the ratio elevated and it instead fell [tr_90ad52897faf]. Logs rule out crash, restart, and intake rejection, and place the break after intake and before payment confirmation [tr_180605051f30]. Traces exclude checkoutservice self-time, the payment/email/shipping/publish legs, currency and catalog fan-out, and the shipping-to-quote hop, leaving cartservice's Redis hop as ~47% of the slow trace [tr_138e08c49752]. GetCart's pre-payment position makes the log truncation follow from a cartservice stall. The change dispatches are exculpatory: checkoutservice has no recorded change over a full day [tr_56d2719f6cfa], and paymentservice's only edits are matched set-then-revert OTLP telemetry changes with no net delta at onset [tr_1f627744be3e]. I blame cartservice rather than the alerting service because a caller stalling silently is what a slow callee produces.
open_questions: No dispatch was run against cartservice or its Redis: no cartservice metrics, logs, or change history exist in this evidence, so blame rests entirely on span attribution seen from checkoutservice's side.
Every returned trace predates onset (23:14-23:34) and only 5 of 30 were returned, truncated [tr_138e08c49752]; the onset mechanism is inferred, not directly observed.

Why the Redis calls slowed is unsettled (memory pressure, connection pool, persistence stall), which also means restart may not be the correct fix; 7 of 10 blast-radius services and 4 unmeasured edges were never examined.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice's Redis ran short of memory, connections, or blocked on persistence, and the ~300ms Redis operations are the symptom of that exhaustion.
alternatives.why_not: No memory, connection, or eviction signal was ever measured on cartservice or Redis; the spans show only waiting [tr_138e08c49752], so exhaustion adds an unobserved claim about why the wait occurs.

alternatives.root_cause: The real stall emerged only after 23:40:15 in a leg absent from the pre-onset trace sample, and the cartservice Redis slowness is unrelated pre-existing noise.
alternatives.why_not: Admitted because all sampled traces predate onset [tr_138e08c49752], but the log truncation point sits exactly at the pre-payment cart phase [tr_180605051f30], which matches the cartservice hop rather than an unseen one.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is predicted. What I would want to see before proposing one: a metric or log dispatch against cartservice and its Redis covering 23:35-23:45 showing cart operation latency (or Redis command latency) departing from its ~22-25ms norm at onset, plus cartservice change history. If cart latency is confirmed elevated at onset, the observable target for any subsequent fix is cartservice GetCart/EmptyCart span duration returning to single-digit-to-low-tens of milliseconds and checkoutservice log lines resuming the full order-start -> payment -> email -> queue sequence rather than truncating at order-start.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if cartservice's Redis stall is in fact a stuck process state that a container recreate would clear, in which case orders continue hanging for the duration of the investigation and the delay is the cost. It would be shown wrong by cartservice evidence naming process-level state - a connection pool exhausted, a persistence fork stuck, a memory-pressure eviction stall - which is exactly the evidence nobody has collected. Note also that the one signal any restart proposal would rest on is unobservable at onset: every returned trace is 23:14-23:34, before the 23:40:15 onset, and only 5 of 30 traces came back truncated [tr_138e08c49752], so the effect of a restart could not be compared against a pre-onset measurement of the thing being fixed.
proposal.risk: Proposing restart_service on cartservice would be an irreversible recreate justified by no cartservice evidence whatsoever. The restart precondition requires evidence pointing at process state; what exists points at Redis operation latency observed second-hand from checkoutservice's span tree, and the verdict itself concedes the mechanism (memory pressure, connection pool, persistence stall) is unsettled - a Redis-side stall is untouched by recreating cartservice's container, so the likely outcome is an outage window with the symptom intact. The three unexcluded mechanisms also differ in whether a restart helps or hurts: if Redis is mid-persistence-stall, dropping and re-establishing every cartservice connection adds load at the worst moment. checkoutservice itself is explicitly not the failing component - error ratio is an eighth of baseline with no sustained departure [tr_90ad52897faf] and no restart or error lines in its logs [tr_180605051f30] - so acting on the seed service would be worse still.
proposal.blast_radius: Nothing changes; no service is touched. For the record, had this proposed a cartservice restart the blast radius would be cartservice plus its inbound callers in this incident's graph - checkoutservice and, through it, frontend and loadgenerator - who would see connection resets during the recreate, and in-flight carts for the orders already hanging at the cart phase would be lost rather than completed.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alert on checkoutservice with loadgenerator following shortly, indicating real user-facing checkout failure rather than a lone synthetic signal. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the many unmeasured dependency crossings mean the cause cannot be guessed from alerts alone.
